clue.text: Person Paris no longer nurtured: old, English, with zero support?

indicators.note: in a down entry a support sits underneath, so the word for zero goes at the bottom, after the rest

parts.note: zero means none, nothing at all

explanation.surface: A riddle about someone the Trojan prince stopped caring for, propped up by nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' places NONE at the foot of the down entry, beneath O and E.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Oenone was the nymph who was Paris's first wife, abandoned when he went off with Helen.

clue.text: Girl's name partly hidden, in actuality

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A girl's name is said to be partly concealed in reality.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also crossword slang for a message hidden in the grid, and this puzzle has one.
explanation.definitionFit: Nina is a common female first name, so it is simply an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Obstacle to soldiers encourages uproar

parts.note: to egg someone on is to encourage them, so encourages gives eggs
hell can mean a noisy uproar or chaos, as in 'all hell broke loose'

explanation.surface: Something blocks the troops and stirs up a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' are not troops but British strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled egg, which must first get through the shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast fingers called soldiers have to break through the hard casing of a boiled egg, so it is their obstacle.

clue.text: Bit of racket in the silence indicating work on farm?

indicators.note: in places that single letter inside the following words
a bit of the word racket is just its opening letter

parts.note: sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A burst of noise breaks a hush, perhaps suggesting farm labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R, the first letter of racket, into THE + SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Threshing, beating grain from the stalks, is a classic agricultural task, hence the question mark for an example.

clue.text: Important teacher picked up dismissing component of education

indicators.note: dismissing tells us to send one item away from the word before it

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so picked up gives heard
R is one of the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, the basics of schooling

explanation.surface: A senior teacher, overheard, sacks part of the curriculum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' removes one of 'the three Rs' (reading, writing, arithmetic) from HEARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The head is the head teacher, the principal of a British school, the most senior member of staff.

clue.text: Dour, sour, nasty — like excrement?

indicators.note: nasty suggests the two words before it are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of unpleasant adjectives building up to something truly foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordure is dung or filth, and the rare adjective formed from it describes something of that nature.

clue.text: This signals puzzling galore with Phi — source of happiness?

indicators.note: puzzling suggests the letters are jumbled into a new, confusing order
the source of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of puzzles galore as a fount of joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzling' rearranges GALOREPHI into HELIOGRAP, and the H from happiness follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A heliograph is an instrument that sends messages by flashing sunlight off a mirror, a device for signalling.

clue.text: University in peak position: new perception

indicators.note: in puts the university letter within the word for peak

parts.note: the acme is the highest point, a peak

explanation.surface: A university perched at the summit gains fresh insight.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen insight or sharp judgement, which is a form of perception.

clue.text: Last of wine provided by vineyard has dull colour

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a cru is a French vineyard or the wine it yields, as in grand cru

explanation.surface: A dull tint from the dregs of the bottle at a vineyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is the pale greyish-beige of unbleached linen, a muted shade.

clue.text: Understood reversed article to be ancient dress

indicators.note: reversed says the word for understood is read backwards

parts.note: if you got something you understood it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something grasped in reverse, with an item, becomes old clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the loose outer garment worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Sound upset, drunk, staggering

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters are reeling about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sounds upset, drunk and unsteady on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'drunk' rearranges SOUNDUPSET, and 'staggering' is not physical but astonishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupendous means astonishingly great, amazing, which is the figurative sense of staggering.

clue.text: Mostly distribute soldiers around one? That sounds bad

indicators.note: mostly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to deal cards is to distribute them

indicators.note: around puts the army corps round the numeral

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Handing out troops around someone draws a pained remark about the situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter; 'around' gives RIEME. 'Soldiers' here is a British Army engineering corps, and 'That sounds bad' is what you say on hearing bad news.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearie me is a mild exclamation of sympathy or dismay, said in response to hearing of a misfortune.

clue.text: Sport, mostly pleasant, involving curious old characters?

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A game, nice enough on the whole, featuring eccentric old personalities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' are not people but letters of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Runic describes runes, the letters of old Germanic alphabets, strange-looking symbols to modern eyes.

clue.text: Enquiring cry? There's nothing in the first room

indicators.note: in puts the zero within the following letters

parts.note: a hall is a large room
A is the first, as in the top grade or the first of a lettered series
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A shout of query, because the main room is empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloa is a variant of hallo, a shout to attract attention or ask whether anyone is there.

clue.text: Banking not about to be providing dodgy data?

indicators.note: not tells us to leave the word for about out

parts.note: banking on something is relying on it
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A bank that is not around supplying fishy figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking' is not finance but 'banking on', depending on.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying means telling untruths, so a liar is supplying false information.

clue.text: Badly convey Mike's opinion

parts.note: Mike is the radio code word for M
an angle is a point of view, an opinion

explanation.surface: Someone garbles what a man called Mike thinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To mangle a message or quotation is to distort or garble it, conveying it poorly.

clue.text: Artist capturing energy in fellow — it's nutty but sweet

indicators.note: in places all that inside the word for fellow

parts.note: man means a fellow

indicators.note: capturing says the artist letters hold the word for energy

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
zip means energy, vigour

explanation.surface: A painter with pep inside some chap: he's crazy but kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Marzipan is a confection of ground almonds and sugar, both nut-based and a sweet.

clue.text: British composer, mentally confused, abandoning carnival city

indicators.note: abandoning says the city is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: delirious means mentally confused
Rio de Janeiro is famed for its carnival

explanation.surface: A British composer, out of his mind, quits the city of samba.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick Delius was an English composer, of works such as On Hearing the First Cuckoo in Spring.

clue.text: Embroil knight in elegant twists

indicators.note: in puts the knight letter among the rearranged ones
twists means the letters of elegant are twisted round

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Drag a knight into some graceful contortions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twists' rearranges ELEGANT and 'in' puts N within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil someone is to involve them in a conflict or tangle, to entangle them.

clue.text: Perhaps Tom's finished the sauce

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, an example, so Tom's gives cat's
up means finished, as in 'time's up'

explanation.surface: The cat has polished off the gravy.
explanation.definitionFit: Catsup is a mainly American spelling of ketchup, the tomato condiment.

clue.text: Sets up European clergy (not men)

indicators.note: not says the word for men is removed

parts.note: rectors are members of the clergy
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, men

explanation.surface: A continental clergy, with men excluded, establishes something.
explanation.walkthrough: '(not men)' removes OR, military shorthand for 'other ranks', from RECTORS.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect something is to build or raise it, i.e. set it up.

clue.text: Fellow's upset about rebuke for heavenly figure

indicators.note: about says the reversed word goes round the rebuke
upset in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: he's is the fellow is
a rap is a reprimand

explanation.surface: A man is distressed by a telling-off from an angel.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upset' turns the letters upwards, giving SEH; 'about' then wraps them round the reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is one of the highest order of angels, so a heavenly being.

clue.text: Island resident against weaponry is penning article

parts.note: anti means against

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the weapon word holds the article

parts.note: gun stands for weaponry, firearms
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An islander opposed to arms is writing an article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing but means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: An Antiguan lives on Antigua, a Caribbean island.

clue.text: Name of Russian beer that is picked up after a kiss

indicators.note: after places the lifted letters following the kiss

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
X represents a kiss, as at the end of a letter

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted, read from bottom to top

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A Russian name for a beer that gets collected after a smooch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' is not a sound clue: in a down entry IE is turned upwards to EI.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexei is a common Russian male first name, as in Alexei Navalny.

clue.text: I scorn struggling to take in difficult English novelist

indicators.note: to take in says the jumbled letters enclose the word for difficult
struggling suggests the letters writhe into a new order

parts.note: hard means difficult

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at a tough English author while battling to read him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges I SCORN to RICSON, and 'to take in' puts HARD within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Richardson wrote Pamela and Clarissa, and is often called one of the first English novelists.

clue.text: Maori group heads for Hamilton and Auckland, having turned up

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters
turned says the word up is flipped round

explanation.surface: A Maori party sets off for two New Zealand cities and has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A hapu is a sub-tribe or clan within Maori society, a kinship group.

clue.text: Wanted to dump man in fact

indicators.note: to dump says the word for man is thrown out

parts.note: desired means wanted
sir is a form of address for a man

explanation.surface: Wanting to ditch a man, in reality.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue ends on 'in fact', but 'in' is only a link; 'fact' alone defines, as in the phrase 'in deed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deed can mean actual fact or reality, as in the phrase 'in deed', contrasted with mere words.

clue.text: Fuel used in older vehicles

indicators.note: used in tells us the answer is sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A fuel that older vehicles burn.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv is British slang for diesel used in road vehicles, from Diesel-Engined Road Vehicle.

clue.text: Power-crazed, facing setback in the rain?

indicators.note: facing setback means the combined letters are turned back to front

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
mad means crazed

explanation.surface: A power-mad person runs into a reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out in the rain makes you wet, and damp means slightly wet.

clue.text: Pressure if parable gets amended in religious document

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: amended says the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Pressure means a parable is revised in some sacred text.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal brief is a formal letter from the Pope, less weighty than a bull, on church matters.
